title: Eclypses Partners with Sterling to Deploy Payload-Level Post-Quantum Cryptography across Federal Systems - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Cybersecurity firm Eclypses has selected federal integrator Sterling to deploy its FIPS 140-3 validated MicroToken Exchange (MTE) payload-level post-quantum cryptography across U.S. federal agencies, positioning to capture demand ahead of the October 22, 2026 OMB M-26-15 PQC migration-plan deadline.

insights.claim: Eclypses has selected IT integrator Sterling to deliver its patented MicroToken Exchange (MTE) platform to U.S. federal government agencies, combining Eclypses' quantum-resistant data protection with Sterling's federal systems integration practice.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals a channel play to monetize federal PQC mandates through an established integrator rather than direct sales.
insights.quote: Cybersecurity technology developer Eclypses has selected IT solutions integrator Sterling to deliver its patented MicroToken Exchange® (MTE) platform to U.S. federal government agencies.

insights.claim: The joint go-to-market platform is led by Eclypses CEO David Gomes and Sterling CTO Chris Cyr, enabling defense and civilian agencies to secure production data environments while meeting federal PQC compliance targets.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Named executive sponsorship indicates a strategic, not tactical, commitment to the federal channel.

insights.claim: MicroToken Exchange replaces sensitive data payloads with single-use, self-verifying, non-mathematical tokens at the application layer, so intercepted packets contain no reusable keys or certificates and are unusable to adversaries employing cryptanalytically relevant quantum computers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Payload-level tokenization is differentiated from network-transport (TLS/IPsec) PQC approaches and targets the harvest-now-decrypt-later threat directly.
insights.quote: MTE replaces sensitive data payloads with single-use, self-verifying, non-mathematical tokens at the application layer.

insights.claim: The Eclypses platform is powered by the Eclypses Cryptographic Library holding FIPS 140-3 Certificate #4690 and natively incorporates NIST post-quantum standards including ML-KEM (FIPS 203) key encapsulation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: FIPS 140-3 validation and NIST-standard integration are gating requirements for federal procurement.

insights.claim: MTE is distributed as a containerized software package across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and Oracle and integrates into existing legacy systems and API endpoints within hours without requiring network re-architecture or code rewrites.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Low-friction deployment lowers the adoption barrier for agencies racing against migration deadlines.

insights.claim: Under OMB Memorandum M-26-15, issued June 2026, all federal civilian executive departments and agencies must submit comprehensive post-quantum cryptography migration plans by October 22, 2026, within 120 days of release, establishing roadmaps for High Value Assets.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A hard federal deadline creates a near-term demand catalyst for compliant PQC vendors.
insights.quote: all federal civilian executive departments and agencies must submit comprehensive PQC migration plans within 120 days of release, establishing actionable roadmaps for High Value Assets (HVAs).

insights.claim: Sterling will incorporate Eclypses MTE into its federal PQC practice alongside asset discovery (Eracent), network visibility (Gigamon, Fortinet), and AI workload verification (Quantum Helix AI Identity) to provide automated cryptographic inventory, gap analysis, and zero-trust modernization.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Positions Eclypses within a broader multi-vendor federal PQC stack rather than as a standalone point tool.
